text:
julia_sales: Heads up — PulseMed renewal coming up. They're on a $500k annual commit today. Asked to rebaseline to $750k with a 20% off-list concession if they sign a 36-month term. They also want data-residency carveouts for EU workloads. @nina_dealdesk

sam_pre_sales: Do we have monthly token profile? I saw episodic spikes for image+text workloads. That matters for dedicated sizing.

julia_sales: T12 tokens ~220B, avg month ~18B, peak 42B last December. They plan to add multimodal endpoints which will increase GPU hours.

nina_dealdesk: Two flags: 1) 20% off at that scale normally needs RevOps + CRO approval 2) 36-month term with price locks needs legal check on escalation and repricing triggers.

diego_finance: From a recognition view, multi-year prepay changes ARR patterns. If they prepay, we'll need to amortize revenue; if annual payments, different. Also need to model churn exposure.

julia_sales: Customer preference is annual invoices but wants guaranteed rate for 36 months. Also asked for an overage cap and lower per-1M token overage rate once above commit.

sam_pre_sales: Technical ask: they want dedicated instance pools in eu-west and us-east with reserved NVMe and pinned GPUs. That increases infra cost; propose adding a hardware surcharge or adjusting discount.

omar_csm: CSM side: must include migration window & runbook, plus a 45-day validation period for any residency move. Also request on-call escalation list and quarterly health checks.

contracts_bot: Reminder — include contract id, proposed concession table, and security exceptions when submitting for review: https://redwood-internal/dealsubmit

nina_dealdesk: Suggest two proposals to execs: A) Flat 20% off for 36 months with a 10% hardware surcharge for residency OR B) 15% off with staged uplift: Year1 $600k, Year2 $725k, Year3 $750k and capped overage at $5/1M tokens above threshold. Which do we prefer?

julia_sales: Customer pressed on predictability — leaning A if we can push residency surcharge low. They also want a clause for model upgrade protection (no surprise repricing for minor model improvements).

diego_finance: Finance prefers staged (B) to reduce revenue risk. Can we add an earnout credit if usage exceeds X% so we get committed revenue?

sam_pre_sales: For A, infra team must confirm eu-west pool capacity and NVMe availability. If we can't guarantee pinned GPUs we should not promise residency.

omar_csm: Also add a rollback plan: if residency migration causes issues, customer wants a 14-day rollback without penalty. Need to check legal.

nina_dealdesk: I'll open a strategic rate exception and mark for CRO review. Action items: Julia attach T12 usage + contract id, Sam confirm infra capacity, Omar attach runbook requirements, Diego provide revenue modeling for both options.

julia_sales: Adding docs now. Also they asked for a 30-day POC extension to validate multimodal latency with a 20M token cap. They want that included in SOW as a free validation period.

contracts_bot: Note — any free-validation environment must be conditional on signed MSA and limited in scope.

diego_finance: If free POC included, include a clause that it's trial-only and not production-grade; costs count toward consumption if extended.

nina_dealdesk: Will draft two concession tables and a recommended approval path. Expect draft for review tomorrow AM.

julia_sales: Thanks. I'll sync with PulseMed CFO about payment cadence (annual vs prepaid) and push back on the broad price-lock asks. :thumbsup:

sam_pre_sales: I'll ping infra and post capacity update here.

omar_csm: I'll start a template runbook and collaboration checklist for residency migration.

nina_dealdesk: Closing note: include any regulatory attestations (HIPAA/GDPR language) in the request if PulseMed needs them.

julia_sales: On it. Will upload security questionnaire answers and proposed SOW clauses once I have them.
